text: If statements let your program make decisions, running code only when a condition is true.
Age is twenty, which is greater than or equal to eighteen, so that condition is true and we print Adult.
The else block is the fallback — it runs only when the if condition turns out false.
When you have more than two paths, use elif to add extra branches, [shush] checked one at a time, top to bottom.
The moment one condition matches, Python runs that block and skips all the rest entirely.
You can combine conditions with and, or — here both temperature over seventy and sunny must be true.
And is strict, needing every part true, while or is generous, needing just one.
[sigh] If statements can also nest inside each other, checking a second condition only after the first one passes.
[chuckle] And for the simplest either-or choices, the ternary expression squeezes a full if-else onto one tidy line.
